newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan labour credit unions to discuss mergers.
newsitem.headline: Japan labour credit unions to discuss mergers.

text.p: Leaders of Japanese labour credit unions in western Japan are expected to hold a news briefing later on Thursday relating to mergers among several credit unions in the region, industry sources said.
The Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper reported that seven credit unions, which serve members of labour unions, in six prefectures in western Japan have agreed to merge on an equal basis in October 1998.
"It is true that we had a meeting yesterday about it (the merger)," an industry source said. "We are preparing to hold a news conference today."
The Yomiuri Shimbun said the seven credit unions will set up a committee and soon start negotiations with the Finance and Labour ministries about mergers aimed at improving their financial strength.
Of the seven credis unions, two are located in Osaka and the rest are in Kyoto, Hyogo, Shiga, Nara and Wakayama prefectures, it said.
The value of deposits for the seven totalled 1.08 trillion yen and the number of offices stood at about 80 at the end of March.
